faq.title: Before you turn a reference into your next script.
faq.description: What copywriters and marketers usually want to know before analyzing or adapting a sales message.

analysisAndAdaptation.question: What exactly do I get from Kyrg Studio?
analysisAndAdaptation.answer: Choose analysis to uncover the hook, structure, offer, persuasion, proof, objections, and weak points inside a sales message. Choose adaptation to use those insights as the strategic foundation for a new script built around your own offer.

supportedFiles.question: Is adaptation the same as copying someone else's VSL?
supportedFiles.answer: No. Kyrg Studio studies how the reference builds its argument and persuasion, then applies that strategic logic to the audience, promise, proof, and constraints of your offer. The goal is a new script, not a reproduction of the original wording or claims.

processing.question: Do I need to be an experienced copywriter to use it?
processing.answer: No. The result is organized so marketers, producers, and founders can understand the reasoning behind the message. Experienced copywriters can use it to accelerate research and diagnosis, while still applying their own judgment to the final copy.

closeBrowser.question: How long does it take, and do I need to keep the page open?
closeBrowser.answer: Processing time varies with the length of the reference and the result you request. You do not need to watch the screen: after submitting the file, you can close the page and return later to see the result in your account.

uploadedFile.question: What happens to the video or audio I upload?
uploadedFile.answer: The original media is used only while your analysis or adaptation is being processed. When processing finishes or cannot be completed, the uploaded file is removed. Your structured result remains available in your account.

offerProfile.question: What should I provide to get a strong adaptation?
offerProfile.answer: Describe your audience, the problem they face, the outcome they want, your promise, mechanism, benefits, objections, available proof, offer terms, tone, and restrictions. The more specific and truthful your profile is, the more useful and consistent the adapted script can be.

inventedInformation.question: Will it invent testimonials, guarantees, or results?
inventedInformation.answer: Kyrg Studio is designed to work only with the proof and offer details you provide and to flag important information that is still missing. Because every AI-assisted draft can require context and judgment, you should review claims, numbers, and commercial terms before publishing the final script.

productOffer.title: Product and offer
productOffer.description: Explain clearly what you sell and what result it helps the customer achieve.

product.label: What product or solution are you offering?
product.description: Include the type of product, its purpose, and the transformation it provides.
product.placeholder: Example: An online English conversation course for Brazilian adults.

audienceProblem.title: Audience and problem
audienceProblem.description: Describe the person this message should reach and the main problem they are trying to solve.

audience.label: Who is the target audience?
audience.description: Include relevant characteristics, context, experience, and current situation.
audience.placeholder: Example: Brazilian adults who understand English but freeze when speaking.

problem.label: What is their main problem?
problem.description: Focus on the most important difficulty the offer addresses.
problem.placeholder: Example: They have studied for years but cannot speak naturally in real situations.

desirePromise.title: Desire and promise
desirePromise.description: Define what the audience wants and what your offer can responsibly promise.

desire.label: What does the audience most want?
desire.description: Describe the result, feeling, or situation the audience wants to reach.
desire.placeholder: Example: Speak English confidently in everyday and professional situations.

promise.label: What is the main promise?
promise.description: Use a realistic promise that your product can support without exaggeration.
promise.placeholder: Example: Build the confidence and practical ability needed for real conversations.

mechanism.title: Unique mechanism
mechanism.description: Explain what makes the approach different and why it may work better for this audience.

field.label: How does your solution work?
field.description: This field is optional. Describe a real method, process, framework, or differentiator without inventing claims.
field.placeholder: Example: Conversation practice based on situations the student encounters in everyday life.

benefits.title: Benefits
benefits.description: Add the most important practical or emotional benefits provided by the offer.

list.label: What benefits can the customer expect?
list.description: Use one clear benefit per item. Avoid promises that the product cannot support.

objections.title: Objections
objections.description: List the doubts, fears, or reasons that may stop the audience from taking action.

list.label: What objections does the audience have?
list.description: Use one objection per item and write it from the customer's perspective.

proofAssets.title: Available proof
proofAssets.description: Add only evidence that already exists and can be verified. The adaptation must not invent testimonials, numbers, or results.

list.label: What evidence supports the offer?
list.description: Examples include real testimonials, case studies, demonstrations, credentials, or documented results.

offerTerms.title: Price and conditions
offerTerms.description: Describe the real commercial details that the adapted message may present.

field.label: What are the offer details?
field.description: This field is optional. Include price, payment terms, access period, bonuses, guarantees, or relevant conditions.
field.placeholder: Example: Twelve months of access, payment in up to 12 installments, and a seven-day guarantee.

callToAction.title: Call to action
callToAction.description: Explain clearly what the audience should do after watching or listening to the adapted message.

field.label: What action should the audience take?
field.description: Use a specific action that matches the real purchasing or contact process.
field.placeholder: Example: Click the button to learn more about the course and enroll.

toneLanguage.title: Tone and output language
toneLanguage.description: Define the intended voice of the adapted copy and the language of the final script.

tone.label: What tone should the copy use?
tone.description: Describe the desired communication style using a few clear characteristics.
tone.placeholder: Example: Direct, welcoming, confident, and conversational.

language.label: What language should the final script use?
language.description: Use a language or locale such as English, Portuguese, pt-BR, or es-MX.

platformDuration.title: Platform and duration
platformDuration.description: Define where the copy will be used and the approximate length of the final script.

platform.label: Where will this copy be used?
platform.description: Examples include Instagram, YouTube, a sales page, webinar, or paid advertisement.

duration.label: Desired duration in minutes
duration.hint: Use decimal values when needed, such as 1.5 for one minute and thirty seconds.

restrictions.title: Restrictions
restrictions.description: Define the boundaries the adapted script must respect.

list.label: What must the adapted copy avoid?
list.description: Add prohibited promises, unsupported claims, sensitive topics, words, or approaches that should not appear.
